<description>
Guix release binaries use GCC’s POSIX thread model, while the pinned Nixpkgs toolchain defaults to mcf. This makes POSIX the default for Nix Windows cross builds. Nightly builds can select `mcf` or `win32` with the `threadModel` argument.

The Nixpkgs `threads` setting selects the model before GCC is built. Only the mcf model pulls in `mcfgthreads`. For POSIX, GCC’s target libraries need winpthreads headers and libraries during the compiler build. The `EXTRA_*_FOR_TARGET` flags provide those paths without exposing target headers to GCC’s native build tools, which caused the earlier build failure.

The compiler wrapper includes winpthreads through `extraPackages`, so the shell no longer needs to export pthread include and library flags manually. CI also prints GCC’s configured thread model to make mismatches visible.

Fixes #36314
</description>

<commits>
96d487c11e ci: raise BuildKit step log limit

The Windows cross-toolchain build can exceed BuildKit's default 2 MiB
per-step log limit, which hides useful output.

Raise the limit to 5 MiB for both CI builder configurations. This
retains substantially more diagnostics without enabling unlimited logs.

1d59d5ad25 ci: use POSIX threads in Nix Windows cross shell

Guix release binaries use the POSIX GCC thread model, but the pinned
Nixpkgs cross compiler defaults to MCF. Select POSIX through the
Nixpkgs threads hook so GCC and its target libraries agree.

Leave threads.package null because making winpthreads a target
dependency exposes its headers to native GCC build tools. Supply its
headers and libraries through EXTRA_*_FOR_TARGET for target libraries
instead.

Add winpthreads to the compiler wrapper so builds in the shell get
its include and library paths without manual NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE or
NIX_LDFLAGS exports.

9fd18aedb0 ci: print Windows cross compiler thread model

BuildKit can truncate the compiler build log, hiding its configure
flags. Print the compiler version and thread model when CI enters the
Nix test shell so a mismatch is visible in the job output.
</commits>

diff --git a/ci/test/02_run_container.py b/ci/test/02_run_container.py
index d726b36a44..d91d60a510 100755
--- a/ci/test/02_run_container.py
+++ b/ci/test/02_run_container.py
@@ -191,7 +191,7 @@ def main():
             "nix-shell",
             f"{os.environ['BASE_ROOT_DIR']}/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix",
             "--run",
-            f"exec bash {shlex.quote(test_script)}",
+            f"echo 'Windows cross compiler:' && \"$CXX\" -v && exec bash {shlex.quote(test_script)}",
         ])
     else:
         ci_exec([test_script])
diff --git a/.github/actions/configure-docker/action.yml b/.github/actions/configure-docker/action.yml
index 074b47ce34..a447741a0a 100644
--- a/.github/actions/configure-docker/action.yml
+++ b/.github/actions/configure-docker/action.yml
@@ -14,10 +14,14 @@ runs:
       with:
         driver-opts: |
           network=host
+          env.BUILDKIT_STEP_LOG_MAX_SIZE=5242880
 
     - name: Set up Docker Buildx
       if: ${{ inputs.provider != 'warp' }}
       uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
+      with:
+        driver-opts: |
+          env.BUILDKIT_STEP_LOG_MAX_SIZE=5242880
 
     # This is required when using the gha cache backend with a manual docker buildx invocation.
     # Docker will check for variables $ACTIONS_CACHE_URL, $ACTIONS_RESULTS_URL and $ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN
diff --git a/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix b/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix
index 4fd83b0da7..559c4312b5 100644
--- a/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix
+++ b/contrib/devtools/shell-win64-cross.nix
@@ -9,24 +9,38 @@
 
 let
   host = builtins.getEnv "HOST";
-  crossPkgs = if host == "x86_64-w64-mingw32ucrt"
+  baseCrossPkgs = if host == "x86_64-w64-mingw32ucrt"
     then pkgs.pkgsCross.ucrt64
     else if host == "x86_64-w64-mingw32"
       then pkgs.pkgsCross.mingwW64
       else throw "Unsupported HOST: ${host}";
+  crossPkgs = baseCrossPkgs.extend (_: _: {
+    threads = {
+      model = "posix";
+      package = null;
+    };
+  });
   toolchain = crossPkgs.stdenv.cc.targetPrefix;
   pthreads = crossPkgs.windows.pthreads;
+  crossGcc = crossPkgs.buildPackages.gcc14;
+  gcc = crossGcc.override {
+    cc = crossGcc.cc.overrideAttrs (old: {
+      # Keep target pthread headers out of GCC's native build tools.
+      env = old.env // {
+        EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET =
+          "${old.env.EXTRA_FLAGS_FOR_TARGET} -idirafter ${pthreads}/include -B${pthreads}/lib";
+        EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET =
+          "${old.env.EXTRA_LDFLAGS_FOR_TARGET} -Wl,-L${pthreads}/lib";
+      };
+    });
+    extraPackages = [ pthreads ];
+  };
 in
 
 pkgs.mkShellNoCC {
-  packages = [
-    crossPkgs.gcc14
-    pkgs.nsis
-  ];
+  packages = [ gcc pkgs.nsis ];
 
   shellHook = ''
-    export NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE="-isystem ${pthreads}/include $NIX_CFLAGS_COMPILE"
-    export NIX_LDFLAGS="-L${pthreads}/lib $NIX_LDFLAGS"
     export CC=$(command -v ${toolchain}gcc)
     export CXX=$(command -v ${toolchain}g++)
     export LD=$(command -v ${toolchain}ld)

</patch>
